checks: No eclipse at 1 of 3 covered epochs where the 61.87899 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.

timing.note: only 2 fully-covered eclipse(s) in the data - at least 3 are needed to test the period for timing changes

writeup: TIC 403329469 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 61.878992 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.05%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 22.0. However, the eclipses show significantly alternating depths - a pattern suggesting the true period is twice the initial measurement - which was flagged by data quality checks. No secondary eclipse detection and this alternating-depth pattern remain open questions about the system's nature. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find in the automated survey.
